content.subject: Proposed changes to the agreement
content.body:
Hi,

I hope you’re well. Before I sign the agreement, I would like to request a few modest adjustments for clarity and balance:

- The current termination clause allows the Client to end the agreement without cause and only pay for work already performed. I propose that either party may terminate with thirty (30) days written notice only if the other materially breaches, and otherwise termination should include mutually agreed compensation for work performed and reasonable costs incurred.
- The invention assignment clause makes all inventions developed during the project the Client’s exclusive property, even if I have not been fully paid. I suggest that I retain ownership of all inventions and grant the Client a non‑exclusive, royalty‑free license to use them for the Services, unless we agree on separate compensation.
- The IP clause states that all deliverables are works made for hire and belong to the Client regardless of payment. I recommend that ownership of deliverables transfer to the Client only after full payment for the services that produced them; until then, I retain all right, title, and interest.
- The conflict‑of‑interest clause gives the Client the unilateral right to terminate immediately without liability. I propose that either party may terminate upon written notice of a material conflict of interest, provided the terminating party pays for all services performed up to the effective termination date.

Thank you for considering these revisions. I look forward to finalizing the agreement.

Best regards,
